shisper.title: Shisper surged far beyond its 1997 outline

points.t: the tongue ends near its 1997 RGI outline (yellow).
ice has pushed well past that outline into the main valley — the 2018–20 surge.
surging ice dammed the valley and caused the Hassanabad outburst floods, even while GB as a whole loses ice.

shisper.note: Shisper's 2000–2019 mean dh/dt is +0.10 m/yr because the surge thickened the tongue; 2015–19 −0.05 m/yr.

passu.title: Passu: the tongue holds its place but thins

points.t: the clean-ice tongue ends close to its 1997 outline at all three dates; no clear advance or retreat at this zoom.
surface change went from +0.02 m/yr (2000–04) to −0.42 m/yr (2015–19) — the ice is losing height, not length.
Passu is clean ice, so its Sentinel-2 snow percentages are not interpretable.

batura.title: Batura: the tongue keeps its length, loses height

points.t: the debris-covered tongue fills its 1997 outline to the end at every date; the earliest frame is a mixed Landsat and Maxar mosaic.
surface change went from +0.12 m/yr (2000–04) to −0.26 m/yr (2015–19).
end-of-summer snow on the glacier fell from 71 % (2019) to 65 % (2026); 2025 was the lowest.

hispar.title: Hispar: the fastest thinning of the six

points.t: the terminus sits near its 1997 outline at all three dates; no clear length change at this scale.
+0.07 m/yr in 2000–04 became −0.86 m/yr in 2015–19, the fastest of the six key glaciers.
end-of-summer snow fell from 75 % (2019) to 58 % (2026), the only statistically significant decline (p 0.03).

biafo.title: Biafo: a debris-covered snout that hides its losses

points.t: the rubble-covered terminus sits on its 1997 outline at every date (2019 is Earth's newest high-resolution tile here).
+0.17 m/yr in 2000–04 turned to −0.17 m/yr in 2015–19: debris cover slows retreat, so loss shows up as lowering.
end-of-summer snow on the glacier fell from 87 % (2017) to 79 % (2026), with 2025 the lowest.

baltoro.title: Baltoro: GB's largest glacier holds near balance

points.t: the debris-covered snout sits on its 2002 outline at every date (2019 is Earth's newest high-resolution tile here).
surface change −0.06 m/yr (2000–04) and −0.05 m/yr (2015–19) — the 'Karakoram anomaly' at work.

points.b: But the snow line is rising:
points.t: end-of-summer snow fell from 81 % (2017) to 72 % (2026); the snow line rose to 4,800 m in 2025–26.
